pages_convention: XML section and paragraph locators (jats_text) for the abstract and captions (§0 ¶1, Fig. N, Table N as printed). The XML text has no body, so body text is cited by printed journal pages, which equal PDF pages counted from 1 (p. N). Body quotes are copied from the PDF.

entry.evidence: analysis of a Mw 5.3 earthquake that occurred near Bhachau on 14 June 2020

sequences.source_document: Choudhury et al. 2022 published PDF (body) with XML abstract and captions

steps.action: Report the published rival views on the 2001 Bhuj causative fault: the hidden North Wagad Fault (Rastogi et al.) versus the South Wagad Fault with NWF as a branch (Biswas 2005).
steps.quote: Biswas (2005) opined that South Wagad Fault (SWF) is the causative fault of the 2001 Bhuj earthquake

steps.action: Set the aim: locate the 2020 main shock and aftershocks, determine their depths and focal mechanisms, and test the fault-branching suggested by previous studies.
steps.quote: especially to test branching of faults as suggested by many previous studies

steps.action: Describe the GSNet broadband and strong-motion network (60 BBS, 45 telemetered), the 2019 50-station offline array, and the SEISAN location procedure with a regional 1-D velocity model.
steps.quote: The network can reliably detect earthquakes of M2.0 in the Kachchh region and M2.5 in other areas of Gujarat.

steps.action: Summarize the GSNet catalogue since 2007 (about 20,000 shocks) and map Kachchh seismicity concentrated along ABF, GF, SWF and KMF, with the KMF-SWF transfer zone the most active.
steps.quote: seismicity is mostly concentrated along ABF, GF, SWF, and KMF

steps.action: Take the 14 June 2020 Mw 5.3 Bhachau event as a live event recorded by the dense network, and assign macroseismic intensity (MMI VII) from felt reports and damage.
steps.quote: The Mw 5.3 earthquake occurred at 20:13 hrs (IST) on 14 June 2020.

steps.action: Locate the main shock (focal depth 19.9 km) and invert four-station broadband waveforms with ISOLA (discrete wavenumber Green's functions, regional 1-D model, filtered displacement) for a moment tensor: reverse faulting with a small strike-slip component.
steps.quote: The FM derived from the moment tensor shows a reverse fault with a small strike-slip component

steps.action: Compare the 2020 mechanism with the 2001 Bhuj mechanism and the regional tectonic trend: similar reverse faulting, but a sinistral rather than dextral strike-slip component and an ESE-WNW plane.
steps.quote: this mechanism is somewhat similar to that of the 2001 Bhuj earthquake, but the nature of the strike-slip component is different

steps.action: Locate the aftershock-period events (37 events in 10 days; 433 or 434 events up to June 2021) using the array together with GSNet; depths are 5-30 km.
steps.quote: We also used data from 50 BBS array network (Fig. 2b), together with that from GSNet to constrain the hypocentral locations.

steps.action: Compare the depth distribution with the regional seismogenic depth and the depth section with the known faults SWF, KMF and NWF.
steps.quote: The depth section reveals that these earthquakes are associated with known faults like SWF, KMF and NWF in the Kachchh rift

steps.action: Propose that the post-2020 events are not all aftershocks of the Bhachau main shock, given the region's background productivity.
steps.quote: we speculate that the sequence of all the earthquakes (Table 2) is not the aftershocks of the 2020 Bhachau earthquake

steps.action: Estimate magnitude of completeness and Gutenberg-Richter b-value for the sequence with ZMAP, using maximum likelihood.
steps.quote: The Mc and b-value for this sequence were found to be 1.6 and 0.67 ± 0.04, respectively

steps.action: Compare the sequence b-value with the published whole-KRB value and read it as a higher probability of large events.
steps.quote: the b-value of this sequence is smaller than that for the whole KRB (1.05 ± 0.05, Singh et al., 2012)

steps.action: Fit the modified Omori law to the 380-day sequence, giving a decay exponent p = 0.46.
steps.quote: for this sequence is estimated as 0.46 (Fig. 5b)

steps.action: Compare p with the typical aftershock value (~1) and read the rate and magnitude-time plots: two decay trends and random large events, so no smooth main shock-aftershock decay.
steps.quote: the seismicity does not follow a main shock-aftershock behaviour (Omori’s law)

steps.action: Estimate focal mechanisms of the M > 3.5 post-main-shock events with the same moment tensor method: reverse with strike-slip, and pure strike-slip.
steps.quote: The FMs of M > 3.5 earthquakes that occurred after the 2020 Bhachau earthquake have also been estimated using the same methodology

steps.action: Reject the reading that all events are aftershocks of the Mw 5.3, on the evidence of the differing mechanisms and the frequency-magnitude-time distribution.
steps.quote: This is validated by the FMs (Fig. 4a) and the distribution of frequency and magnitude as a function of elapsed time

steps.action: Place the Mw 5.3 hypocentre and its MT strike and dip (118°, 64°) on the south-dipping SWF within the Kothyari et al. double fault zone.
steps.quote: the hypocentre of the Mw5.3 earthquake falls on the south dipping SWF, which is a part of the double fault zone

steps.action: Assign faults: the Mw 5.3 is not a 2001 aftershock; the Mw 4.6 on the Kanthkot fault and the Mw 4.1 on a N-S transverse fault are triggered events; the Mw 3.5 and 3.6 events lie on the north-dipping KMF.
steps.quote: This is triggered by the Mw5.3 earthquake and is not an aftershock

steps.action: Set the results against published regional stress inversions, magnetotelluric and tomographic images of deep faults, double-fault-zone stress transfer, and GPS strain rates; report all as consistent.
steps.quote: This aspect is also supported by previous geophysical studies

steps.action: State the conclusions: the sequence occurred in the SWF double fault zone, it triggered two M > 4 events, mechanisms fit regional transpression, and the hazard continues.
steps.quote: The 14 June 2020 Mw5.3 earthquake and the subsequent ones occurred in the SWF double fault zone, where intermediate stress is accumulated.

tree.answer: Yes: an M ~ 4 event almost yearly in the Samakhiali basin, and earlier M ≥ 5 events
Not tested: no sensitivity, alternative-model or independent-data checks performed
Best explanation: SWF double-fault-zone rupture with triggered events on nearby faults

end.claim: The 14 June 2020 Mw 5.3 Bhachau earthquake ruptured the south-dipping SWF in its double fault zone with reverse, slightly strike-slip motion, and triggered M > 4 events on nearby faults rather than producing a simple aftershock sequence.

decisive_move.sentence: The hypocentre location and ISOLA moment tensor inversion of the main shock and the M > 3.5 events are what allow the events to be assigned to the SWF, the Kanthkot fault and the KMF.

gates.evidence: The data come from routine monitoring of a natural event (p. 3); no hypothesis directed their acquisition. The non-aftershock reading meets Omori and b-value statistics and differing mechanisms (pp. 4-5), and the fault attribution could have failed had the hypocentres not fallen on mapped faults (p. 6), but neither is framed as a test with a failure criterion. Nothing was fixed in advance; the frequency band was 'set variably' per event (p. 3).

imports.item: Maximum likelihood estimation (applied to the b-value through Utsu 1978)

limits:
The XML text holds only the abstract and captions, so body steps are cited by PDF page. No review file was supplied, so there is no review sequence.

The stated aim to 'test branching of faults' (p. 2) is never explicitly resolved; the paper adopts the branching picture of Kothyari et al. and Biswas (inference).

No V check is performed here. The waveform fit in Fig. 3 (variance reduction) is goodness of fit, not a check. The 'validation' by focal mechanisms and statistics (p. 5) is coded as the evidence of the X step, not as V, because both analyses produced the claim. The only consistency checks are against cited independent studies (Joshi et al. 2017; MT and tomography studies).

The moment tensors come from four stations, with no uncertainty or sensitivity reported.

Internal inconsistencies:
- The abstract counts '20 aftershocks' (M 2.0-4.6) in 10 days; the body counts 37 events (M 1.1-4.6).
- The abstract counts 129 tremors to June 2021; the body says more than 400.
- The text analyses 433 events; Table 2 totals 434.
- The abstract gives 5 nano-strain/year; the body gives 0.05 micro-strain/year (50 nano-strain/year).
- The intro says an M ~ 5 event 'almost after 8 years'; the conclusions say 'after 19 years'.
- The abstract calls the events aftershocks; the body argues they are not all aftershocks.

The dense-GPS recommendation is future work and is not coded as a step.

Sub-claim statuses:
- b-value 0.67 ± 0.04 and Omori p = 0.46: estimate_with_resolution.
- Main-shock mechanism: estimate without stated uncertainty.
- Triggered-not-aftershock reading of the Mw 4.6 and 4.1 events: best_explanation (weakly supported, inference).
- Higher probability of large earthquakes from the low b-value: an interpretation, untested.

disagreements.target: Aftershock behaviour expected under the modified Omori law (Utsu 1961), p ~ 1
disagreements.support: The fitted p = 0.46, the two-trend rate decay and the random timing of large events are read as non-aftershock seismicity.
disagreements.quote: It is also observed that the seismicity does not follow a main shock-aftershock behaviour (Omori’s law).

disagreements.target: Rastogi et al. (2013a): the 2001 main shock on the hidden North Wagad Fault
disagreements.support: The paper adopts the view of Biswas (2005) and Kothyari et al. that NWF branches from SWF and places both the 2001 and 2020 events in the SWF zone, without a new test of the 2001 fault.
disagreements.quote: The 2001 Bhuj and the recent 2020 Bhachau earthquakes have occurred on the SWF zone

alternatives_considered.chosen: Post-2020 events are not all aftershocks; the Mw 4.6 and 4.1 events are triggered events on nearby faults
alternatives_considered.alternatives: An aftershock sequence of the Mw 5.3 main shock
alternatives_considered.reason: Differing focal mechanisms, low Omori p, and the frequency-magnitude-time distribution

alternatives_considered.chosen: NWF as a subsidiary branch of SWF, with SWF as the master fault
alternatives_considered.alternatives: NWF as the causative fault of the 2001 earthquake (Rastogi et al., 2013a)

v_checks.quote: The depth distribution is consistent with the seismogenic depth in the Kachchh region (Joshi et al., 2017).
This aspect is also supported by previous geophysical studies
